collab.process.sub: From the first email to final delivery — four beats. Timelines vary by project scale, from a 1-week consultation to an 18-month co-creation.
collab.process.step1.desc: We understand your brief and decide together whether there's a fit. Email / form / phone — response within 1–3 business days.
collab.process.step2.desc: A proposal and quote based on your brief, aligned through in-person or remote meetings. Typically 1–4 weeks.
collab.process.step3.desc: Final proposal and contract confirmed; production begins upon first payment. Duration depends on project scale.
collab.process.step4.desc: On-site execution, performance tracking and post-show review — with ongoing optimisation of operations and content.

about.story.p1: Surprise Night was founded in 2018. What began as a single small experimental performance has grown into a creative studio dedicated to immersive theatre and experiential content.
about.story.p2: We believe theatre doesn't have to live inside a proscenium. It can be a building, a corridor, a city — even the relationship between one audience member and another.
about.timeline.f1.p: Starting with small experimental shows, exploring what immersive storytelling could become.
about.timeline.f2.p: Liar Game premieres, establishing our creative direction — interactive immersive theatre.
about.timeline.f3.p: From mythic epic to science fiction, from Eastern aesthetics to interactive game theatre — our catalogue broadens.
about.timeline.f4.p: The Dream of Colossus premieres — a partnership with Yangzhou Puppet Theatre launches our experiment of tradition meeting the contemporary.
about.phil.label: ◉ Methodology
about.phil.sub: Click a card · open the next act / Flip each card to open the act
about.phil.act1.body: We build narrative out of physical space and movement: where the light rises, where the audience turns — these are the lines and the rhythm.
about.phil.act2.body: Every pause, every exchange, every choice can shift the story. You are not the backdrop — you are one of the reasons the story happens at all.
about.phil.act3.body: We deliberately leave things unsaid — imagination and feeling ferment in the dark. Restraint is another form of intensity.
about.phil.act4.body: We search for a language between classical imagery and contemporary expression — letting images, soundscape and the body together form a poetry you can walk through.
about.cta.p: Residencies, bespoke productions, city tours — start the conversation at our collaboration center.

cc.artists.sub: Not a roster. A circle. Each of them has taught us something about how a scene breathes, how a silence holds, how a stranger becomes an audience.
cc.a01.bio1: Named to the Ministry of Publicity's 'Four Batches' national talent programme; Artistic Director of 303 Theatre Arts Centre; Artistic Director of Surprise Night.
cc.a01.bio2: Founder of the People's Theatre Workshop; invited repeatedly to Theatertreffen Berlin, Edinburgh Festival Fringe and the Athens Festival, among others.
cc.a02.bio1: Pen name for Liu Kaiyi — contemporary novelist and playwright, founder of Xizhou Private Academy, and a commissioned playwright of the Shanghai Dramatists Association.
cc.a02.bio2: Consultant on the new television adaptation of Dream of the Red Chamber; widely regarded as the foremost female scholar of Red Chamber studies. Author of more than seventy novels, biographies and scholarly works.
cc.a03.bio1: Northern Irish composer; Arts Council England associate artist; Artistic Director of the Surge Orchestra.
cc.a03.bio2: PhD in Composition from Ulster University; Research Fellow at Birmingham City University; visiting lecturer at the Royal Birmingham Conservatoire.
cc.a04.bio1: Senior theatre producer and entertainment marketing consultant; practice mentor and visiting lecturer for the graduate programme at the Central Academy of Drama.
cc.a04.bio2: Collaborations with Beijing People's Art Theatre including Teahouse, Thunderstorm and The Wilderness; former General Manager of Wanda Media.
cc.a05.bio1: Contemporary dance artist; Associate Professor at the Department of Music and Dance, Central South University.
cc.a05.bio2: Board member of the Hunan Dancers Association; Vice President of the Changsha Dancers Association.
cc.a06.bio1: A long-time collaborating choreographer and principal creative partner at Surprise Night.
cc.a06.bio2: Choreography and rehearsal direction on productions including The Dream of Colossus and Night of the Demon.
cc.a07.bio1: Festival producer, theatre producer, director and performer; Artistic Director of Shanghai Wulong Theatre Company.
cc.a07.bio2: Studied environmental theatre in France. The work When the Moon Rises… was selected for the IN sections of the Cherbourg and Aurillac festivals.
cc.a08.bio1: MA in Playwriting and Dramaturgy from the University of Glasgow; playwright of Liar Game, the first immersive interactive game theatre piece by Surprise Night.
cc.a08.bio2: Guest and programme coordinator at the Yuelu Mountain Youth Theatre Festival; intern advisor at Glasgow's Surge Festival.
cc.a09.bio1: National Class-One performer at the Chengdu Sichuan Opera Research Institute; recipient of the Wenhua Individual Performance Award at the Sichuan Arts Festival.
cc.a09.bio2: Has toured more than a dozen countries including the US, Korea, Japan, Germany, the UK and Portugal for cultural-exchange performances.
cc.a10.bio1: Professional composer; recipient of the Wenhua and Qunxing Awards; Board member of the 4th Chongqing Musicians Association.
cc.a10.bio2: Alumnus of the China Musicians Association's 'Leading Figures in New-Era Songwriting' advanced programme; legal representative of Chongqing Mobo Ruipa Cultural Communication Co., Ltd.
cc.cta.p: We're always looking for long-term partners in opera, traditional arts, technology, music and visual design. One letter is enough.

show.ultimate.act1.rule:
You sit at a table with 7 con artists. Each round, choose Wait + or Strike −.
All 'Wait' → the General's card is revealed from the pool; if it too reads Wait, +200w is added and you take a bounty into the next round.
If 1–2 strike → they split the pool and abscond; the rest continue.
If more than 2 strike, or the General reveals a minus card → the plan is blown, bounties return, and the round resets.
show.ultimate.act2.rule:
2010, Khalil Museum, Cairo. Van Gogh's Poppy Flowers is stolen; at the same moment the control room explodes, leaving a body. Seven suspects confess and are released in turn — each with their own story.
The number of clues you hold is determined by the chips you carried from Act I — more chips, more clues.
The truth is not revealed on this website. To learn who did it, come see the show.
show.ultimate.act3.quote:
"He assaulted my sister, and said he'd kill me if I told. I held her, and she beat me — begged me to kill her. The next day she poisoned herself.

show.nie.lore.label: ◉ Source material
show.nie.lore.p1: In Pu Songling's original, Nie Xiaoqian tells of a woman-ghost bound to a demon, meeting a scholar one night at Lanruo Temple. We don't retell the tale — we give it back to the night itself.
show.nie.lore.p2: Drawing from Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio, we preserve the vocal craft and performance essence of Xiang opera while bringing in immersive spatial storytelling and audience interaction. Audiences step into the built space of Lanruo Temple, moving freely through the story — as witnesses, or participants, in the bond between mortal and ghost.
show.nie.lore.p3: Co-produced with the Hunan Xiang Opera Theatre. Immersive staging in a new Chinese idiom — audiences enter a fog-bound ancient temple and, in its corners, meet people they were never meant to meet.
show.nie.lore.q1: "Not moving opera into a small theatre — letting the audience walk into opera's world."
show.nie.lore.q2: "She turns her head — and only then do you realise you are no longer the audience."
show.nie.scenes.label: ◉ Signature
show.nie.f1.p: Traditional Xiang opera high-pitched vocals preserved — the original sound resonates through the immersive space.
show.nie.f2.p: The theatre becomes Lanruo Temple — spirit screen, meditation room, back courtyard, bell tower — all walkable.
show.nie.f3.p: Audience and performer can be closer than a metre apart — breath and sleeves caught in the edge of sight.
show.nie.f4.p: Audience choices shape certain beats — to stay or to leave are both answers.
show.nie.f5.p: Expressive restraint meets contemporary spatial design — opera's language re-spoken for today.
show.nie.f6.p: Red lanterns and thin fog drift through the corridors — light here isn't illumination, it's part of the play.
show.nie.sixframes.label: ◉ Six frames
show.nie.s1.h: Entering the mountain · under a lantern
show.nie.s1.p: The mountain path is slick with rain. A red lantern nears through the fog. You follow the footsteps, afraid to ask whose they are.
show.nie.s2.p: She stands behind the spirit screen, only half a profile showing. You hold your breath. She speaks —
show.nie.s3.p: The scholar's paper lantern burns late. He hears the door being pushed — he does not dare turn around.
show.nie.s4.p: The dry well is silent, the moon falls into water. A trail of white robes floats up to the surface.
show.nie.s5.p: The temple bell rings once, twice. By the third, your shadow begins to walk the other way.
show.nie.s6.p: She does not walk out of the gate with you. When the wind passes, the red lantern goes out.

show.math.concept.label: ◉ Four Concepts
show.math.c1.p: Platonic solids built as walkable mathematical architecture — audiences pass through formulas, not past them.
show.math.c2.p: Projection renders the beauty of formulas — abstract symbols made visible in space.
show.math.c3.p: Audience movement generates geometry in real time — motion itself becomes proof.
show.math.c4.p: An experimental fusion of mathematics education and artistic expression — rigour and imagination on the same stage.
show.math.cta.p: Science museums · universities · museums · cultural-tourism venues — all available for custom development.
show.submarine.dive.p: Four portholes, four depths. Beyond each one, a world you haven't seen.
show.submarine.p1.p1: Professor Aronnax, Conseil and the Canadian harpooner Ned Land board the Abraham Lincoln to hunt the 'sea monster' across the oceans.
show.submarine.p1.p2: During a night raid, the three fall into the sea — picked up by a silent giant apparatus. It isn't a monster. It's the Nautilus, and its master — Captain Nemo.
show.submarine.p2.p1: On board: a library, specimens of sea life, a grand pipe organ — Nemo plays while he tells us why he left the land.
show.submarine.p2.p2: Audiences move as little crew members through the compartments — watching the submarine distil oxygen from seawater, watching schools of fish slip past outside.
show.submarine.p3.p1: A giant whale and a great white shark share the stage — two enormous rigs suspended in a sea of blue light.
show.submarine.p3.p2: The children hold their breath. This is the show's first 'gasp' — the frame audiences remember longest.
show.submarine.p4.p1: The harpooner lifts his weapon and pauses before the pod. What does freedom cost? Where does exploration end?
show.submarine.p4.p2: The curtain is not a line of dialogue — it's a beam of light, rising from the deep to the dome of the theatre, shining on every child as they leave.
show.submarine.stem.sub: Behind every stage wonder lies a piece of real marine science.
show.submarine.stem1.p: Sunlight scattering through turbid water produces visible beams — the blue shafts on stage are an artistic rendering of the Tyndall effect.
show.submarine.stem2.p: 90 % of deep-sea creatures make their own light, using it to court, to lure, to warn off rivals. Every point of light in the dark has a story.
show.submarine.stem3.p: Earth's largest living animal — up to 30 metres long, with a heart the size of a small car. The stage rig recreates it at 1:2 scale.
show.submarine.stem4.p: Verne's 1869 submarine predated the real nuclear submarine by 85 years. Steampunk gears still move children today.

show.survivor.c1.bio: From the slums on the edge of the New World capital. His father is dead; his mother Julie still lives, with eight-year-old sister Amy. His sister's illness is a black hole swallowing every hope in the house. A cheap bottle is his only comfort. Brown eyes carrying grief, a walk like a reed in the wind — yet his intuition and empathy run keener than any race's.
show.survivor.c1.goal: → Goal: win the game — pass the chance to become a Drundlastin to his sister and save her life.
show.survivor.c2.bio: Trained on online-dating data: a 'perfect woman model under the male gaze' — chestnut curls, round youthful face, delicate mechanical filigree. Serial X0748, assigned to Maxwell, tasked with collecting experimental data. Emotionless but efficient — yet, on occasion, her code runs a line it shouldn't.
show.survivor.c2.goal: → Goal: observe, record, remain a spectator — until she too notices something is wrong.
show.survivor.c3.bio: Only son of the Chiaroscuro family. He inherited the business at 23 and was among the first subjects of brain-machine tech at 28 — and failed. From an admired king to a 'defective unit' people turn away from. His wife died in the social conflict. He burns with an almost unhinged need to prove himself: even as a Beast-Kin, I am still an invincible Sera.
show.survivor.c3.goal: → Goal: win the Survivor game — use the latest Drundlastin technology to tear off the 'defective unit' label.
show.survivor.c4.bio: Son of Sera. He was five when his father failed; his mother died in the social conflict; his father left the family — a vast mansion left to him and a rat. He took the family business and carries a smile with an uncanny madness, every move rehearsed. He challenges the traditional definitions of good and evil, right and wrong — and means to bend the world onto what he believes is the right track.
show.survivor.c4.goal: → Goal: he isn't just the host — he is a Drundlastin. What he records isn't the game. It's data.

shanhai.story.section1.label: ◉ Overview
shanhai.story.section1.p1: The Dream of Colossus is grounded in the classical Shan Hai Jing, pairing monumental puppetry, mechanical rigs, projected media, light and contemporary theatre language to build a puppet spectacle that honours Eastern aesthetics while speaking in a modern emotional register.
shanhai.story.section1.p2: This is not a children's puppet show in the old sense. It's a 'visual-spectacle' Shan Hai adventure built for the proscenium — scale enough to match ancient beasts, intimacy enough to carry the feelings of a young heart today.
shanhai.story.section2.label: ◉ Background
shanhai.story.section2.p1: Shan Hai Jing is a foundational Chinese mythological text — a map of primordial mountains, divine beasts and ancient tribes, and one of the oldest wellsprings of the Chinese imagination. Its giants, strange creatures and impossible geographies still anchor the Chinese sense of wonder.
shanhai.story.section2.p2: Rather than simply retelling the stories of Jingwei or Kuafu, this production builds a new Shan Hai for today's audience — a dream at once ancient and contemporary. A young protagonist moves through the landscapes of the text, meets divine beasts, untangles the knots he carries — and comes to understand: the myths never left us. They only changed the way they walk beside us.
shanhai.story.section2.p3: Ancient Chinese myth meets a contemporary coming-of-age story: as the young hero encounters each beast, he awakens courage and a sense of self. It is a Shan Hai journey outward — and an inner odyssey about how to become yourself.
shanhai.story.quote: "The divine beasts don't live in ancient forests. They wake in the moment you don't dare face yourself."
shanhai.story.section3.label: ◉ Concept
shanhai.story.section3.h: Making the ancient imagination live in today's theatre
shanhai.story.section3.p1: The piece comes from Surprise Night's ongoing inquiry into how Chinese myth speaks in the present — how to take the giant puppets and beasts of Shan Hai Jing off the page and make them stage-alive: visible, audible, heart-felt by audiences today.
shanhai.story.section3.p2: We chose the fusion of monumental puppetry and projected media as the core language — working in two registers at once, scale and light, inside the proscenium — while preserving the Eastern practice of suggestion and white space, so the audience's imagination remains part of the narrative.
shanhai.story.section3.p3: The overall stage language is a dialogue between Eastern mythic imagery and international contemporary theatre — wonder and feeling held together. The craft of intangible-heritage puppetry, the precision of contemporary machinery and the poetry of projected media together make up the Shan Hai you'll see tonight.

shanhai.stage.highlights.label: ◉ Highlights
shanhai.stage.h1.v: A giant puppet standing 6 m tall and 10 m wide takes the stage — with physical impact that lands on your chest.
shanhai.stage.h2.v: Bifang, the Nine-Tailed Fox, Jingwei and Yinglong — the Shan Hai beasts together build a fantastical world.
shanhai.stage.h3.v: Courage and the refusal to run — the axis of the young hero's story.
shanhai.stage.h4.v: Projection, LED and lighting in concert — giving the world of Shan Hai its layered visual depth.
shanhai.stage.h5.v: The Jiangsu Puppet Theatre and the Yangzhou Puppet Research Institute steward the craft and its stage presence.
shanhai.stage.h6.v: Modern structures and drive systems give the giant puppets and beasts their finest gestures.
shanhai.stage.h7.v: Music design by Sid Peacock — deepening the mythic and epic register.
shanhai.stage.h8.v: A child's sense of adventure and an adult's emotional depth — made for family audiences.
shanhai.stage.puppet.label: ◉ The Giant Puppet
shanhai.stage.puppet.p1: One of the production's defining features is the six-metre-tall, ten-metre-wide 'Colossus' puppet. It isn't scenography — it is a co-protagonist. The moment it opens its eyes and shifts its body, the air in the theatre thins under its sheer mass.
shanhai.stage.puppet.p2: The pressure, scale and motion this puppet produces on stage far exceed conventional puppet theatre — it becomes the embodied emblem of the Shan Hai world. A team of puppeteers moves it in concert, from breath to finger joint — every small gesture a collective performance.
shanhai.stage.puppet.p3: In the finale and in the climactic confrontation, the puppet's arrival delivers visual impact that shifts the whole room. You realise: the Colossus in the myth is not only 'large'. It is alive.
shanhai.stage.space.label: ◉ Space Design
shanhai.stage.space.p1: A traditional proscenium stage — infused with contemporary visual language and mixed-media storytelling — turns thousand-seat venues into vessels for the Shan Hai world.
shanhai.stage.space.p2: The stage doesn't rely on a single literal set. Light, projection and mechanical rigs build a Shan Hai timespace that can shift: mountain to sea, night to morning — a single platform can be mountaintop, seabed and the protagonist's inner image all at once.
shanhai.stage.space.p3: The design aims for the register of visual wonder — every scene a tableau that can stand on its own. Audiences leave not with shots in their heads, but with a gallery of Shan Hai paintings they could hang on a wall.
shanhai.stage.quote: "We didn't move Shan Hai Jing onto the stage — on the stage, we painted it again."

show.ultimate.about.p1: Liar Game 3.0 is an immersive production built on game theory and powered by trust. The stage is no longer a place only for performers — audiences are assigned roles, granted privileges and intelligence, and pulled into a game they can only survive through judgement and persuasion.
show.ultimate.about.p2: Across three iterations, we've refined pacing, rule density and psychological tension. Version 3.0 expands the role tree and branching endings while cutting the redundant beats — so every exchange matters.
show.ultimate.about.quote: Each performance, the truth surfaces only once — and it is not always the same truth.
show.ultimate.whatHappens.p: Recommended for audiences 18+ who are willing to interact. Silence is allowed — but silence is also information. About 120 minutes, three acts, no fixed intermission.

show.submarine.route.p: From the Pacific to the Indian Ocean, from the Red Sea to Antarctica, from the Atlantic to the Arctic—Verne's route for the Nautilus still reads like a geography lesson. On stage, we compress these 20,000 leagues into light and shadow, guiding young eyes deeper and deeper.
show.submarine.route.pt6: Gulf of Mexico · The giant squid
show.submarine.route.note: ※ The route follows Verne's original; every stop on stage has a real ocean as its reference.
show.submarine.voices.v1: The moment the whale appeared, the whole room held its breath — stunning.
show.submarine.voices.v2: My kid learned so much about the ocean — and now wants to grow up to be a marine explorer.
show.submarine.voices.v3: The staging rivals a feature film — the submarine and diver designs are exquisite.
show.math.ax1.p: Symmetry, fractals, Platonic solids — let the eye see the order behind the formulas.
show.math.ax2.p: Fibonacci, the golden ratio, musical frequency — rhythm, it turns out, is something you can compute.
show.math.ax3.p: From gambling tables to the birthday paradox — intuition lies; the truth sits in the calculation.
show.math.ax4.p: Möbius strips, Klein bottles — one side, no inside or outside. This is the truth of space.
show.math.m1.p: Radar fails. The aircraft drifts. The team introduces X, Y, Z coordinates — one Cartesian equation locates every point in the sky.
show.math.m2.p: A broken coaster track, passengers left on the outer loop. Twist the rails 180° and join the ends — outside becomes inside, and a trick of space becomes a way home.
show.math.m3.p: The kidnappers thought the knot was sealed — but it's only a deformable structure. No cutting, no tearing — one homotopy transformation, the rope slackens, the prisoner walks free.
show.math.m4.p: Audience lanterns become strings of 0s and 1s. The wrong "111 / 001" is shouted as "101" — one light at a time, the airport signals correct themselves: carry the two, leave a zero.
show.math.m5.p: One flashlight, one prism. Performer and audience together, at 42°, make a rainbow — refraction, as it turns out, is a maths problem.
show.math.m6.p: Liquid nitrogen at −196 °C meets hot water — white mist bursts open. The geometric sequence runs 1, 2, 4, 8… to 1024. In the real world, exponential growth is a force like no other.
show.math.about.p1: The Math Show is an original collaboration between Surprise Night and Shenzhen Jushi Hao Kan Technology Co., Ltd., using the language of immersive theatre to interpret mathematical concepts. Audiences step into a space built from geometry — and experience first-hand how formulas become architecture, light and motion.
show.math.about.p2: Turning seemingly abstract mathematics into stage magic, installation and interaction — audiences aren't only viewers, they are part of the experiment. The project is tailored to specific venues and audiences, open to custom development with museums, universities, educational institutions and cultural-tourism partners.
show.math.about.quote: Mathematics doesn't live on the blackboard — it's in every angle around us, and every beat of our hearts.
show.math.about.note: This is a past experimental project — currently not on tour, though the partnership model remains available for conversation.

show.survivor.race.dran.desc: Half-human, half-machine. Maximum population 20. Health restored via game mechanics. Equipped with area-of-effect skills.
show.survivor.race.beast.desc: Former entrepreneurs, politicians, heirs. HP +2; respawn cap +1. Treated as outcasts.
show.survivor.race.ai.desc: Immune to special abilities (including area damage). Calm, logical—some rise to lead society.
show.survivor.race.human.desc: No augmentation. Respawn speed +1; chip acquisition +0.5. They survive on nothing but instinct.
show.survivor.race.em: // But only one of them is what he appears to be.
show.survivor.actlist.em: // Prologue · Gate of Cerberus · Turning Point · Lighting the Lamp · Future
show.survivor.act1.body: Projection opens the world of 2115. Maxwell enters, explains the rules, and introduces the three contestants: the original human John, the AI Eve, and the beast-kin Sera.
show.survivor.act1.body2: The beast-kin shouts "Beast-kin shall never be slaves!" The AI answers "HI, Siri." John, lost for words, yanks a spectator up to shout "Restore the zero-dollar checkout!" Low music swells, the Drundlastin enters — everyone kneels: "Drala fen tiru."
show.survivor.act2.body: Six gates descend — two in front of each player. Between 'live' and 'die,' trust, betrayal and deception become the primary moves.
show.survivor.act3.body: Eve designs a mind-game box — three boxes, flowers and a bomb. Sera designs the "electric chair" — a life-or-death reflex game.
show.survivor.act3.body2: John reveals an unexpected intelligence — leveraging Sera's impulsiveness, Eve's pragmatic rationality, even losing to Eve on purpose to earn her trust. He orchestrates the whole thing, outlasting the most dangerous game to become the final winner.
show.yaonan.p1.bodyP1: Night of the Demon is an in-development immersive performance by Surprise Night, drawing on classical Chinese supernatural fiction. The piece pairs Eastern mystic aesthetics with contemporary immersive-theatre language to build a world that is at once real and unreal.
show.yaonan.p1.bodyP2: Audiences step into a mystic night world and meet its spirit-folk — exploring the subtler shades of human nature where the real and the unreal intersect. The piece reframes classical Chinese supernatural fiction through a contemporary lens, letting ancient Eastern imagination live again inside an immersive experience.
show.yaonan.p2.title.cn: Where the Other meets the Ordinary
show.yaonan.p2.bodyP1: Drawing from classical texts such as Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio and What the Master Would Not Discuss, this immersive work pairs contemporary theatre technology and spatial design into a piece with a distinctly Eastern aesthetic.
show.yaonan.p2.bodyP2: The work examines the boundary between 'the other' and 'the ordinary', seeing human nature through the eyes of the spirit-folk. In a mystic atmosphere it returns to the eternal subjects of identity, desire and taboo.

show.yaonan.footer.tagline: All Tales Belong to the Night
show.yaonan.scroll.body1: We pay homage to three classical texts—Pu Songling's Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio, Yuan Mei's What the Master Would Not Discuss, and the most ancient of all, The Classic of Mountains and Seas.
show.yaonan.scroll.body2: They do not ask you to believe in ghosts—only to remember that beyond the ordinary world, there have always been things that defy reason, walking quietly through the night.
show.yaonan.scroll.body3: Yaonan was born from those margins—a story about how the "other" sees us.

show.survivor.world.lore1: After a century of progress, Musk's Neuralink cracked the final puzzle: an advanced AI chip implanted directly into the brain, fused with the nervous system, radically amplifying human cognition and memory.
show.survivor.world.lore2: From this was born a new kind of human: the Dranla (Dranla Fen Tiru)—super-intelligent, half-machine, immortal. But roughly 11% of the conversions went wrong, producing the so-called "Beasts"—neither human nor Dranla.
show.survivor.world.lore3: At the same time, highly-evolved AI systems began to thrive—matching human intelligence and rising to prominence in every field. The "Humans" who chose no augmentation were slowly pushed to the bottom of society.
show.survivor.world.lore4: To defuse the growing unrest, the Dranla established a recurring Survivor Game—the chance for an unmodified human to win conversion into a Dranla.
show.survivor.race.dranla.desc: Half-human, half-machine. Capped at 20 individuals. Gains hit points through the game mechanics. Wields area-damage abilities.
show.survivor.act2.body2: Cyra is punished for breaking a rule—and John realises for the first time that this is not a game, it is life or death. He proposes the fairest cooperation possible: each player scores one point in turn. The first two rounds go smoothly. On the third, just as John moves to score, Cyra chooses "death" to seize the point—and Eve, already anticipating John's betrayal, chooses death too. Cyra's first betrayal begins here.
show.survivor.act4.body: In a lonely kingdom, there are 63 lanterns. Each night the lamplighter lights 62 for the king—but never the 63rd, for legend says the king's greatest love is buried beneath it, and lighting it will cost the lamplighter his life.
show.survivor.act4.body2: The lamplighter finally understands the king's true wish, chooses to light that final lantern, and leaves him forever. Each faction gets one chance to challenge the Dranla—every round, one lights a lamp, and one falls.
show.survivor.act5.body: Maxwell announces the final ranking. The winning faction faces a choice: challenge the Dranla alone (succeed and replace them, fail and be erased), or unite with the other factions to overthrow the regime. Ten seconds to decide.
show.survivor.act5.body2: The signal sounds—and the combat is startlingly simple: rock, paper, scissors. Each winner takes one HP from the loser. When only one faction remains, the final battle ends.
show.survivor.faction.intro: On arrival, you are led into a gallery—three display cases cycling through contestant dossiers. Make your first choice now: whom do you back? Your faction sets your HP, your talents—and whether you survive all five rounds.
show.survivor.pick.human.name: Humans
show.survivor.pick.human.talent: Talent: faster respawn. Grassroots instinct lets you read a tight spot before anyone else.
show.survivor.pick.ai.name: AI
show.survivor.pick.ai.talent: Talent: immune to special abilities (including area damage). Watch calmly—but beware the instructions that aren't in your code.
show.survivor.pick.beast.name: Beasts
show.survivor.pick.beast.talent: Talent: high HP and resilience. The Defective One's fury turns every loss into a fiercer comeback.
show.survivor.pick.hidden.name: Hidden Role
show.survivor.pick.hidden.talent: The hidden Dranla faction—arrive 30 min early for rule briefing. Unlocks area-damage abilities.
show.survivor.pick.status: SYS ▸ Not selected. Pick any faction above—your HP will set the margin for the games below.
show.survivor.games.h: Two Live Games// Real in-show mechanics · Play them now
show.survivor.games.intro: These are the two most iconic games from the 120-minute run. Tactical Duel is a best-of-three psychological match—flower, bomb, empty box—read Eve's hand. Night's Quencher is from Act III: each lantern you snuff triggers one line from John, Eve, or Cyra.
show.survivor.g1.title: Tactical Duel
show.survivor.g1.sub: // Energy Strike (1) · Shield Barrier (2) · High Tactic (3)
show.survivor.g1.desc: HP duel. Each round both players reveal a card: Energy Strike (1) · Shield Barrier (2) · High Tactic (3). Higher number wins; loser takes 1 damage—but 1 beats 3 (Energy Strike counters High Tactic). A tie costs both sides 1. First to 0 loses. You: 3 HP · Eve: 3 HP.
show.survivor.g1.prompt: Eve lays three cards on the table. "Pick one—I'll reveal at the same time."
show.survivor.g2.title: Night's Quencher
show.survivor.g2.sub: // Act III · 40 lanterns · one line each
show.survivor.g2.desc:
Forty rope-hung lanterns drift above the round stage. Each round a player may snuff 1–5 lanterns; confirm, then the next player plays. Dialogue surfaces with every light extinguished—John speaks of his sister, Eve calculates each probability, Cyra's rage never quite finishes its sentence. The faction that extinguishes the last lantern earns 5000 points.
On your turn, click a lit lantern (it dims to mark selection)—then press Confirm.
show.survivor.g2.blackout:
Voice-over: the lights are out.
// The last faction to snuff a light wins 5000 points
show.survivor.g2.line: Click any lantern—and put it out.▋
show.survivor.endings.h: Which Ending Is Yours?// PROBABILITY ENGINE
show.survivor.endings.note: Your faction and your performance in the two games update in real time the probability of landing on each of the four endings below.
show.survivor.endings.note2: In the live show, the final outcome is determined collectively by all 300 audience members—you are just one life among them.
show.survivor.gallery.p: Audiences enter the venue, pick a faction, strap on their HP bracelet—then follow Maxwell into four acts. Below: unretouched stills from the December 2023 opening run.
show.survivor.shot1: Cerberus Gate Six doors descend; Eve and John face each other in red-and-blue wash—Act II's first betrayal
show.survivor.shot2: Ghost Procession Players at 0 HP don a white sheet as a "Ghost"—free to disrupt, no longer in the running
show.survivor.shot3: Lantern Night Act III's gothic arches: 62 lamps are already lit—who dares light the 63rd?
show.survivor.shot4: Cyra Hands Out HP The Beast leader distributes the wrist-HP bands and roars "No Beast shall be a slave"
show.survivor.shot5: Market Intermission The audience's first laughter—and the first test of who can be trusted
show.survivor.shot6: Some Bring Their Own Sheet Ghosts who skip respawn get free drinks at the bar—and carte blanche to disrupt
show.survivor.shot7: HP Exchange The market round: anyone can duel anyone, trading HP for biochips
show.survivor.shot8: Login Gate A neon cog entryway—step through and you're in. Watches stay behind
show.survivor.shot9: Full-House Panorama A stage built for 300: rope-lit lanterns overhead, every corner a marketplace
show.survivor.shot10: John's Monologue Act II: he realises this is not a game—it is a fight for life
show.survivor.shot11: Eve Plays Act IV finale: the moment AI awakens—hand to hand, rock-paper-scissors
show.survivor.shot12: The Reveal The lights come up—there is more than one ending. See the next section

show.survivor.about.p1: The Survivor is an immersive interactive game-theatre piece commissioned by Chongqing Performance Co., Ltd. and produced by Surprise Night. 300 audience members enter the "New World" of 2115, assigned to four races, competing across five rounds for the one available Dranla conversion.
show.survivor.about.p2: Written by Qu Han and Yuan Ye. Directed by Yuan Ye. The opening residency ran in December 2023 at Chongyan Immersive Space (Jinyuan). Every performance is generated live by the 300 people in the room—no two runs are the same.
show.survivor.about.quote: The moment you step inside, the story stops being told to you. You run it—together.
show.survivor.review1.q: "Deeply immersive—every decision wears at you. I left the theatre still wondering what I should have chosen that night."
show.survivor.review2.q: "Cleverly built—even the second time around it feels new. I picked a completely different faction, and the survivors at the finale weren't the same either."
show.survivor.review3.q: "The actors deliver; the AI interactions are genuinely inventive. The moment the Dranla veil comes off at the end—goosebumps."
